challenges.name: Frost Streak
challenges.note: Nine correct actions in a row

hazards.engine-intake-spray-hazard: That aims the spray straight into the engine intake. Fluid pulled into a running or soon-to-run engine does not clean anything — it is exactly the kind of contamination the pass is supposed to avoid, on a part of the aircraft this crew has no business spraying at all.
hazards.ground-personnel-in-spray-hazard: Somebody who is not part of the spray crew is standing inside the boom's own swing radius. The basket moves through a wide arc at height, and a person under it has nowhere to go the moment that arc swings toward where they are standing.
hazards.no-ppe-spray-hazard: You are running the boom without the chemical-resistant suit and respirator on. De-icing fluid drifts as a fine mist the whole time the boom is spraying, and skin contact or breathing it in over a full shift is exactly what that PPE is there to stop happening at all.
hazards.skip-clean-check-hazard: That releases the aircraft without checking the surfaces are actually clean. A wing that looks clear from the ground can still be holding frost in a spot the pass did not fully reach, and the only way to know for certain is the check this crew is about to skip.

interrupts.alert: A gust has pushed the fluid spray back toward the truck cab, well outside the pattern the pass was aimed at.
interrupts.cue: Hit the boom stop now, before the blowback reaches anyone at the truck.
interrupts.missNote: The boom kept running while the blowback reached the truck itself. Fluid that ends up somewhere it was never aimed is exactly the exposure this crew's own PPE cannot fully protect against if it keeps happening.
interrupts.why: A pattern that has drifted this far off target is no longer a controlled pass — it is fluid landing somewhere nobody planned for it to land, and the boom stops the instant that happens rather than continuing on the assumption the wind will settle back down.
interrupts.wrongNote: Not the fix — the blowback reaching the truck is the thing that stops this pass first.

interrupts.alert: A coworker has walked into the boom's own swing radius to check something on the far side of the truck.
interrupts.cue: Stop the boom now and get them clear before it swings again.
interrupts.missNote: The boom kept swinging while a coworker was inside its own radius. A basket at height does not announce itself before it reaches somewhere a person already is.
interrupts.why: The swing radius is not a suggestion — it is the space the basket physically occupies at some point in every full pass, and the one defence against a person inside it is a boom that stops moving the instant they are seen there.
interrupts.wrongNote: Wrong move — somebody is in the swing radius, and that is what stops the boom, not this.

lateNotes.frost-patch-wing: The surfaces get checked by eye and by hand before the holdover clock starts, not assumed clean because the pass looked thorough from the truck.
lateNotes.holdover-panel: The holdover time gets communicated to the flight deck the moment the last fluid application ends, not estimated later from memory.

name: De-icing Truck Boom Operations

passRule.note: stars >= 2 and no unsafe action (WebXR/shared/records.js passed())

steps.cue: Chemical-resistant suit, face shield and respirator before the boom moves.
steps.prompt: Chemical-resistant suit, face shield and respirator before the boom moves.
steps.title: Suit up for the pass
steps.why: A de-icing pass puts this crew directly in a fine drifting mist for the length of the whole spray, in a way a normal ramp job does not, and the suit and respirator are matched to that specific exposure rather than borrowed from a general PPE kit.

steps.cue: Confirm the fluid type, the mix ratio and the holdover chart reference before staging anything.
steps.prompt: Confirm the fluid type, the mix ratio and the holdover chart reference before staging anything.
steps.title: Read the de-icing plan
steps.why: The plan is what ties today's fluid mix to today's actual conditions, and a crew running a pass without reading it first has no way to know whether the holdover time they are about to quote the flight deck even applies to the fluid going on this aircraft.

steps.cue: Walk the truck and boom. Three problems are hiding — find them by looking.

decoyNotes.sound-fluid-tank: The fluid tank gauge reads normal with no leak at the fitting. Nothing to flag there.

itemNames.boom-hydraulic-leak: hydraulic leak at the boom joint
itemNames.heater-fault: fault light on the fluid heater

itemNotes.boom-hydraulic-leak: A leak at a boom joint is control this crew is losing over exactly the arm they are about to swing over a parked aircraft.
itemNotes.cracked-nozzle: A cracked nozzle sprays an uneven pattern, and an uneven pattern is a wing that reads clean from the truck while still holding frost somewhere the check has to catch.
itemNotes.heater-fault: Fluid applied at the wrong temperature does not perform the way the holdover chart assumes it does, which makes the fault light this crew's one warning before the chart's own numbers stop meaning anything.

steps.prompt: Walk the truck and boom. Three problems are hiding — find them by looking.
steps.title: Inspect the truck and boom
steps.why: A boom that looks ready from the ground is not the same thing as one a competent person has actually walked before it swings over a parked aircraft — a leak, a cracked nozzle or a heater fault found now costs a repair, and found mid-pass costs a spray this crew cannot trust the coverage of.

steps.cue: Clear every vehicle and person who is not part of the spray crew, then cone the boundary.

itemNames.cones-deice: cones set at the pad boundary
itemNames.pad-clear: pad cleared of other ground equipment

steps.prompt: Clear every vehicle and person who is not part of the spray crew, then cone the boundary.
steps.title: Clear the pad
steps.why: Everyone and everything inside the pad the moment the boom starts moving is inside the one area this pass is going to put fluid, wind gusts and a swinging basket into, and clearing it first is what keeps that area matching the one the plan actually accounted for.

steps.cue: Drive the truck to the pass position alongside the aircraft.

drag.missNote: Not on the pass position — bring the truck fully into position before raising the boom.

steps.prompt: Drive the truck to the pass position alongside the aircraft.
steps.title: Position the truck
steps.why: The boom's own reach only covers the pattern the plan calls for from one specific position — a truck parked a little off that mark is a pass that either cannot reach part of the aircraft or has to be run twice to cover what the first position missed.

steps.cue: Turn the raise lever to bring the boom up to the pass position.
steps.prompt: Turn the raise lever to bring the boom up to the pass position.
steps.title: Raise the boom
steps.why: The boom has to clear the aircraft's own structure before it ever swings toward it, and raising it fully to the pass height first is what keeps the first swing from being the moment this crew discovers it was not high enough.

steps.cue: Confirm the fluid type and mix ratio match the plan before the pass starts.
steps.prompt: Confirm the fluid type and mix ratio match the plan before the pass starts.
steps.title: Set the fluid mix
steps.why: The mix ratio is what the holdover chart's own numbers are built around — a pass run on the wrong mix is a holdover time the flight deck is about to be quoted that does not actually apply to the fluid now on the aircraft.

steps.cue: Spray the wings first, then the fuselage, then the tail — top-down, clear of every intake.
steps.outOfOrderNote: Wings, then fuselage, then tail — top-down, the order the plan runs the pass in.
steps.prompt: Spray the wings first, then the fuselage, then the tail — top-down, clear of every intake.
steps.title: Run the pass top-down
steps.why: Top-down is the order that lets fluid already applied keep draining clear of surfaces still to be sprayed, rather than running back down over a wing this pass already finished — and every intake on the aircraft stays outside the pattern the whole time.

steps.cue: Read the mix ratio gauge and commit only once it is inside the plan's band.

gauge.label: FLUID MIX
gauge.missNote: Outside the plan's band — confirm the mix ratio before continuing the pass.

steps.prompt: Read the mix ratio gauge and commit only once it is inside the plan's band.
steps.title: Check the mix ratio
steps.why: The gauge is the one number that tells this crew the tank is actually delivering the mix the plan called for, rather than a ratio that drifted while the pass was already running.

steps.cue: Hold the basket control steady through the pass, watching the pattern the whole time.
steps.holdBreakNote: Let go of the basket control mid-pass. Hold it steady — that is what keeps the pattern matching the coverage the holdover time assumes.
steps.prompt: Hold the basket control steady through the pass, watching the pattern the whole time.
steps.title: Hold the basket steady
steps.why: A basket that drifts mid-pass is a pattern that no longer matches the one the plan called for, and holding it steady is what keeps every part of the surface getting the coverage the holdover time is about to be calculated against.

steps.cue: Check the wing and tail by eye and by hand — two spots are still holding frost.

decoyNotes.clean-panel: This panel is clean and dry to the touch. Nothing to flag there.

itemNotes.frost-patch-tail: The tail's own surfaces get the same check as the wings — contamination anywhere on a lifting or control surface is contamination the flight crew needs to know did not happen.
itemNotes.frost-patch-wing: A patch this small is exactly what a pass can miss and a ground check by eye and by hand is built to catch before it matters.

steps.prompt: Check the wing and tail by eye and by hand — two spots are still holding frost.
steps.title: Check the surfaces are clean
steps.why: A wing that reads clean from the truck can still be holding frost in a spot the pass did not fully reach, and the only way this crew actually knows before releasing the aircraft is checking it by eye and by hand rather than trusting how the pass looked going on.

steps.cue: Communicate the holdover start time to the flight deck the moment the last application ends.
steps.prompt: Communicate the holdover start time to the flight deck the moment the last application ends.
steps.title: Start the holdover clock
steps.why: The flight deck is timing their own departure against this exact moment, and a holdover start that is estimated or given late hands them a clock that no longer matches the fluid actually protecting the aircraft.

steps.cue: Turn the lever back to lower and stow the boom before the truck moves.
steps.prompt: Turn the lever back to lower and stow the boom before the truck moves.
steps.title: Stow the boom
steps.why: A boom left raised is a truck that cannot move without striking something overhead, so it comes all the way down and stows clean before this truck goes anywhere else on the ramp.

steps.cue: Log the fluid type, the mix ratio and the holdover start time before signing off.
steps.prompt: Log the fluid type, the mix ratio and the holdover start time before signing off.
steps.title: Log the de-icing pass
steps.why: The next crew and the flight deck's own dispatch release both read this record rather than ask this crew what happened — a pass that went perfectly but never gets logged leaves the holdover clock with nothing behind it but this crew's memory of when it started.
